text:
alyssa: Quick sync — I opened a PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123) to add concrete curl + python examples for exporting audit logs with retention and redaction flags. Need reviews on both wording and the snippets.

kai: Thanks! Can you paste the snippets here? I want to validate SDK parity and surface any header/auth differences.

alyssa: sure — draft curl and python below. The idea is to show `?retain=30d` and `redact=true` as query params, and also an example of server-side redaction header.

alyssa: ```bash
# curl example: export audit logs for tenant `acme-corp` for 30 days, with redaction
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export?tenant=acme-corp&retain=30d&redact=true" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"format":"ndjson","since":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"}'
```

kai: OK that maps fine to the SDK. For python we usually use named params instead of query strings in examples to show the client method:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.audit.export(
    tenant_id='acme-corp',
    retain='30d',
    redact=True,
    format='ndjson',
    since='2026-03-01T00:00:00Z'
)
print(resp.download_url)
```

mohit: Quick security notes: 1) We can't recommend customers set retention longer than their legal need in SOC2 docs — better to say "configure retention per your policy; example uses 30 days". 2) Redaction needs a note: "server-side redaction removes PII fields and is subject to both privacy and completeness trade-offs". 3) For export endpoints, call out that exported files are stored temporarily (24h) and access is logged.

alyssa: Good points. I'll change the copy to: "Example: export audit logs (example uses 30 days). Configure retention according to your organization's policy." And add a short callout about export TTL and access logs.

lex: From Legal: prefer neutral phrasing for SOC2: "We retain operational logs for security, troubleshooting, and compliance. Customers can configure retention windows; example demonstrates a 30-day window." Avoid words like "we keep forever". Also add an optional section: "If you need longer retention for legal reasons, contact support or your account team."

alyssa: Will update. One more SDK nit @kai — can we include an example of the redaction policy payload? like `redaction_policy: "pii-only"` or similar so customers know we support predefined policies.

kai: Yes — backend accepts `redaction_policy` with values `pii-only`, `full`, `none`. Suggest a short example snippet:```json
{ "redaction_policy": "pii-only" }
```

mohit: Also add a small table (one-liner) describing each policy and the tradeoffs: pii-only = removes name/email/ssn; full = attempts to mask all user-provided content; none = no redaction (suitable only for secure internal exports).

alyssa: Perfect. I'll push an update to the PR today with: revised SOC2-friendly copy, curl + python examples, `redaction_policy` options, and an explicit export TTL note.

docbot: automated-check: link-check failed for https://docs.redwood.ai/export-guides (404) — suggest updating link in the PR.

alyssa: acked, will fix links. Anyone else want to weigh in before I request reviews?

lex: sgtm from Legal after the phrasing tweak.

kai: sgtm from SDK side — minor nit: show `resp.status_code` check in python.

mohit: sgtm security; maybe include short sentence about encryption-in-transit and at-rest for exports.

alyssa: great — I'll incorporate all and push a new commit. Thanks! :tada:

kai: thanks, ping me once updated and I'll do SDK parity check.

mohit: thanks — I'll scan for any accidental claims about SOC2 scope in the rest of the docset once updated.

alyssa: will do. closing thread once PR is updated.
